historical_references.reference: The Hindu name Toshif is a variant of the Persian name Tusif, meaning 'pure, chaste, and sinless'. It was adopted by some Hindus during the Muslim rule in India, particularly in the Deccan region.
historical_references.context: During the Muslim rule in India, many Hindus adopted Muslim names to assimilate into Muslim society and avoid discrimination. The name Toshif is an example of this assimilation, reflecting the cultural exchange between the two communities.

historical_references.reference: Another reference suggests that Toshif may have been a title given to Hindu rulers or administrators during the Muslim period, particularly in the region of Malwa in present-day Madhya Pradesh.
historical_references.context: The title Toshif may have been conferred upon Hindu rulers or administrators as a mark of respect or as a way to distinguish them from other officials. This use of the name is less common than the adoption of Toshif as a personal name, but it highlights the complexity of interfaith relations during this period.
